design.title: Widening SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics into the single typed-storage field-type registry
design.summary: SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics today knows only 3 things (Canonicalize, IsDisplayOnly, IsFileLike) and is consulted by only 2 callers (SubmissionFieldNormalizer, SubmissionFileMetaExtractor). Meanwhile the same field-type classification is hard-coded in at least 8 other places: the C# SSR renderer whitelist+switch, the C# ResolveDataType map, the DNN AI DDL classifier, three TS AI skip-sets, and the two TS renderers. Each carries its own spelling assumptions, so aliases drift — most concretely, a field of Type "FileUpload" (emitted by ProposalStarterService) is never rendered as a dropzone by any of the 3 renderers because none canonicalize it before their type switch, which silently breaks upload + MF_Files linkage. The fix is to widen the class into the one registry (add IsDataCarrying, IsStructuredJson, IsConsentLike, IsExternalDataDisplay, CanonicalDataTypeFor + expanded seed sets), route every hard-coded list through it, and create a small TS twin (field-type-semantics.ts) so the two renderers and the TS skip-sets stay in parity with Core per the CLAUDE.md two-renderer rule. This also resolves a live classification drift where PhonePro/PhoneNumberPro map to String but PhoneIntl maps to Json for the same widget.

design.recommendation: Widen SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics into the ONE registry in three moves: (1) Add the 5 requested members + expanded seed sets and two new alias entries (PhoneNumberPro/PhonePro -> PhoneIntl) to resolve the live String-vs-Json drift. (2) Route every typed-storage/render/file classifier through it: SubmissionFieldNormalizer.ResolveDataType delegates to CanonicalDataTypeFor and IsNonDataField to !IsDataCarrying; FormHtmlRenderer canonicalizes before its NativeTypes lookup and RenderInput switch (fixes the FileUpload render bug); DNN IsLayoutOrSkippableType/MapFormTypeToSql reuse the registry. (3) Create a small TS twin renderer/field-type-semantics.ts (canonicalize/isFileLike/isDisplayOnly/isDataCarrying/isStructuredJson) mirroring the C# seeds, and wire it into inputs.ts + megaform-renderer.ts (canonicalize before switch) and the three TS skip-sets — this satisfies the CLAUDE.md requirement that the two renderers stay in parity. Ship all C# targets building clean and keep public submit + builder flow; add a unit test asserting a FileUpload-typed field renders a dropzone and produces an MF_Files row end-to-end.

Replace IsNonDataField (220-228) with: return field==null || !SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics.IsDataCarrying(field.Type); (this now also excludes Row/FlexGrid/Column/Image the old list missed). Leave the raw==null && IsDisplayOnly/IsExternalDataDisplay guard at :128 (unchanged behavior). Optionally move IsSensitiveField (230-236) onto the registry as IsSensitive={Password,Signature}.

Canonicalize before every type decision. In AnyHydrationWidget (105) use NativeTypes.Contains(SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics.Canonicalize(type)). In RenderInput (563-565) set `var type = SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics.Canonicalize(field.Type ?? "Text");` so case "File" (637) matches a FileUpload field and emits the .mf-file-dropzone the JS binder needs. (Add `using MegaForm.Core.Services.TypedSubmission;`.) This is the concrete render-bug fix.

Rewrite IsLayoutOrSkippableType (825-839) as: var t=SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics.Canonicalize(type); return SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics.IsStructural(t)||SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics.IsExternalDataDisplay(t)||SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics.IsFileLike(t)||SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics.IsStructuredJson(t); (fixes the wrong 'GridRepeater=SQL display' comment while preserving the skip). In MapFormTypeToSql (841-870) canonicalize first and, where possible, derive from CanonicalDataTypeFor (Number->DECIMAL, Date->DATE/DATETIME2, Boolean->BIT, LongText->NVARCHAR(MAX), String->NVARCHAR).

NEW small file (per keep-TS-files-small rule) = the TS twin of the C# registry: export const ALIASES={FileUpload:'File',DateTimePicker:'Date',PhoneNumberPro:'PhoneIntl',PhonePro:'PhoneIntl'}; export function canonicalizeType(t){return ALIASES[(t||'').trim()]||(t||'').trim();} plus isFileLike/isDisplayOnly/isExternalDataDisplay/isDataCarrying/isStructuredJson mirroring the exact same seed sets. Single source both TS renderers + skip-sets import.

At renderInput (464-490) compute `const t = canonicalizeType(field.type);` and `switch(t)` so case 'File' (590) handles FileUpload — parity with the FormHtmlRenderer.cs fix. Do the identical change in megaform-renderer.ts renderInput switch (1908). Keeps bindFileUploads (interactive.ts:956) working because the dropzone is now emitted.

Apply the same replacement to the two copies in dashboard/ai-form-creator.ts (2123, 2364) so all three TS skip-sets share the one twin.

risks: CanonicalDataTypeFor needs the Options-count for the Checkbox group-vs-toggle branch; passing hasOptions keeps the signature pure, but any caller that has only a type string (AI DDL) must decide Checkbox=Boolean by default — verify the DNN MapFormTypeToSql Checkbox->BIT stays correct.

Widening IsNonDataField to !IsDataCarrying now also skips Row/FlexGrid/Column/Image which the old 4-item list did not explicitly skip; confirm FlattenFields already descends Row columns (it does) so no child fields are dropped, only the container rows.

Adding File to StructuredJson means File is now true for BOTH IsFileLike and IsStructuredJson; any consumer wanting 'json but not file' must combine the two predicates — document the intentional overlap.

Canonicalizing PhonePro/PhoneNumberPro->PhoneIntl changes their DataType from String to Json for existing forms; on typed-storage-collapse (Oqtane) that alters where the value lands — needs a reader-path/backfill check for any existing PhonePro submissions, or gate the alias behind a saveFormat check.

The two TS renderers must be rebuilt to all 4 wwwroot targets (npm run build) or the SSR (C#) and client (TS) canonicalization will be out of phase — a deploy-skew that reintroduces the exact drift being fixed.
No TS twin exists today; the new field-type-semantics.ts must be kept byte-for-byte in sync with the C# seeds — add a comment cross-reference in both files and ideally a parity test.
open_questions: PhoneIntl: is DisplayValue-based phone search (already implemented per MEMORY typed-DisplayValue hybrid) sufficient, or should saveFormat='e164' fields be classified String for a true sargable phone column? CanonicalDataTypeFor can't see widgetProps.saveFormat from a type string alone — does the normalizer path have the field.WidgetProps available to branch on it?

Should IsSensitiveField (Password/Signature) also move onto the registry as IsSensitive, or stay local to the normalizer?

Do the Oqtane and Web AiToolsController controllers have their own C# DDL classifier twin, or do those platforms run the app-batch DDL entirely client-side through ops-app-batch.ts? (Only the DNN controller currently carries IsLayoutOrSkippableType/MapFormTypeToSql.)

corrections: CONTRADICTION THAT BREAKS A TEST: the proposed IsNonDataField => !IsDataCarrying(field.Type) makes display-only widgets NON-data, because IsDataCarrying excludes IsExternalDataDisplay and ExternalDisplay is defined to contain DisplayOnly {DataRepeater,QRCode} plus DynamicLabel. So a DataRepeater/QRCode/DynamicLabel is now skipped UNCONDITIONALLY at SubmissionFieldNormalizer.cs:119, pre-empting the raw==null guard at :128 that the design explicitly promises to leave 'unchanged behavior'. Those two statements cannot both hold. Fix: IsNonDataField must exclude ONLY IsStructural (layout/presentational), NOT IsExternalDataDisplay, so the raw==null guard at :128 still preserves a display-only widget that DOES carry a value.

TS skip-set replacement is NOT behavior-preserving for Signature. All three current TS sets (ops-app-batch.ts:334-336, ai-form-creator.ts:2123 and :2364) explicitly include 'Signature', but the proposed predicate `!isDataCarrying || isFileLike || isStructuredJson` does NOT skip Signature (it is data-carrying LongText, not in FileLike/StructuredJson/Structural/ExternalDisplay) — so Signature (a base64 data-URL) would become an INSERT/DDL column. Either add Signature to the skip predicate or state and accept this as an intentional change; the claim that the three sets can all 'share the one twin' unchanged is false.

Phone reclassification has DNN-DDL consequences the design never traces (only the Oqtane-collapse storage-location risk is noted). Adding PhoneIntl to StructuredJson AND aliasing PhonePro/PhoneNumberPro->PhoneIntl makes the rewritten AiToolsController.IsLayoutOrSkippableType return TRUE for those fields (via IsStructuredJson), so phone fields are now SKIPPED entirely from AI-generated tables; today `phonepro` produces a real NVARCHAR(40) column (MapFormTypeToSql:852) and would be dropped, and that case becomes dead code. Also note the phone-pro widget is RETIRED (registers as 'PhoneNumberPro' at megaform-widget-phone-pro.ts:1046; JS/CSS removed from the build per loader/index.ts:94,516 and _index.ts:226), and 'PhoneIntl' is a C# FieldType enum value (FormSchema.cs:205), not the widget's registered spelling — so 'live classification drift for the SAME widget' overstates it.

ResolveDataType delegating to CanonicalDataTypeFor(field?.Type, field?.Options?.Count>0) drops the current field==null => SubmissionDataType.String early return (SubmissionFieldNormalizer.cs:24); a null field would canonicalize to '' and hit the switch default => Json. Preserve the null=>String guard.

Compile detail omitted: SubmissionFieldTypeSemantics.cs currently only `using System; using System.Collections.Generic;`. CanonicalDataTypeFor returning SubmissionDataType requires `using MegaForm.Core.Models;` (or fully-qualifying it).

Minor factual slips: (a) the old IsNonDataField (line 224-227) ALREADY skipped 'Row' — it 'missed' FlexGrid/Column/Image/Heading/Divider/HtmlBlock, not Row. (b) The three TS skip-sets are NOT identical to the DNN IsLayoutOrSkippableType: TS carries Section/Razor/File/Signature and lacks Column, while DNN carries Column and lacks Section/Razor/File/Signature — so routing all through one registry changes each surface's skip behavior, it does not merely dedupe identical lists.
missed_call_sites: MegaForm.Core/Utilities/MegaFormUtils.cs:497-503 — DescribeSnapshotValue (inside BuildSubmissionSnapshots) is a fourth C# type-classifier the design never mentions: it hard-codes File/Image => DescribeFileValue and DataGrid/GridRepeater/DataRepeater => DescribeGridValue, with the SAME FileUpload alias gap (matches only 'File', not 'FileUpload'). It is a submission-value display classifier that should also route through the registry or it keeps drifting.

MegaForm.Core/Models/FormSchema.cs:198-210 — the canonical C# FieldType enum uses PhoneIntl / Terms / Country, i.e. the OTHER half of the spelling drift the design describes on the TS side (TS registers TermsPrivacy at _index.ts:513 and the PhoneNumberPro widget). The design cites the TS spellings only and never reconciles them with this enum, which is the authoritative C# vocabulary the normalizer switch is really keyed to.

MegaForm.DNN/Views/FormView.ascx.cs:1931-1938 — a per-type asset-loader switch (case 'datagrid' etc.) is another hard-coded type list; it governs which widget JS/CSS to load rather than typed storage, so it is lower priority, but the design's enumeration of type switches should acknowledge it exists.
verdict.test_impact: Exactly one existing automated test breaks: MegaForm.Sdk.Tests/TypedSubmissionStorageTests.cs `Normalize_DisplayOnlyWidget_WithValue_IsNotDropped` (line 381-399) asserts a DataRepeater field carrying a value still yields one write; under the proposed IsNonDataField => !IsDataCarrying, DataRepeater is now skipped at :119 so writes is empty and Assert.Single fails. `Normalize_DisplayOnlyWidget_WithNoValue_IsSkipped` still passes. The ResolveDataType_MapsFieldTypes theory (lines 16-53) does NOT break: none of its 30 cases are PhonePro/PhoneNumberPro/PhoneIntl, and every tested type maps identically once the switch moves into CanonicalDataTypeFor (Signature=>longtext, File/FileUpload=>json, DateTimePicker=>date, etc.). SubmissionFieldTypeSemanticsTests and SubmissionFileMetaExtractorTests (incl. the existing FileUpload_alias test) are unaffected as long as IsDisplayOnly/IsFileLike are kept for back-compat and the FileLike set is unchanged. No C# test covers the TS DDL Signature/phone changes, so those regressions would ship silently.

design.title: Single-row CLR-list JSON reconstruction limitation: fix design & A-vs-B decision
design.summary: Confirmed: a grid/repeater arriving as a genuine CLR IEnumerable (List/array) with EXACTLY ONE complex row is flattened by SplitRawValue into one JSON row, and CollapseJson's count==1 branch parses that single row and returns a JObject instead of a JArray, silently losing array-ness. Multi-row CLR lists (count>1) and the browser happy path (client sends a stringified array as ONE JSON string, brackets intact) both reconstruct correctly as JArray. The critical blast-radius fact: on the real collapsed-Oqtane read path, TypedFieldValues is rebuilt entirely from DB value rows, so any transient in-memory flag on the write is lost — a correct fix must either be a PERSISTED column on MF_SubmissionFields or be inferred from the already-persisted FieldType, otherwise it only turns the unit test green while the live Oqtane bug remains. Today the bug is largely latent because DNN keeps DataJson and most consumers (reports/CSV/workflow) still read DataJson (reader-switch is backlog), and the browser never triggers it. Given the typed-storage phase is unfinished (Umbraco twin, reader-switch, backfill all pending), I recommend Option B now — ship the missing browser-1-row JArray proof test plus an executable pin-test of the limitation, and document it in the handoff/memory — and pre-design Option A (persisted IsCollection marker) to land together with the reader-switch, when the JObject/JArray distinction actually reaches consumers and the 3-platform migration is done once.

findings.claim: SplitRawValue flattens a genuine CLR collection (List/array that is not string/dict/JObject) into one string part PER ITEM, so a one-element list yields exactly one JSON row with no array brackets.

A single Dictionary row -> ["{\"sku\":\"A1\",\"qty\":2}"], Count==1.

findings.claim: ExtractTypedValues Json branch copies each part into JsonValues 1:1, so a single-row CLR list produces JsonValues.Count==1.
findings.evidence: MegaForm.Core/Services/TypedSubmission/SubmissionFieldNormalizer.cs:205-214 (`foreach (var p in parts.Where(x => x != null)) values.JsonValues.Add(p);`).

findings.claim: CollapseJson treats count==1 as a scalar: it parses the single row and returns whatever token it is (a JObject for one grid row), never wrapping into a JArray. Only count>1 forms a JArray.

findings.claim: Browser happy path is unaffected at ANY row count because the client submits a stringified array as ONE string; SplitRawValue skips the IEnumerable branch for strings and returns the whole '[...]' as one row, which CollapseJson parses to a JArray.
findings.evidence: SubmissionFieldNormalizer.cs:290 guard `!(raw is string)` skips arrays-as-strings; falls to 298-300 returning ["[{...}]"]. Reconstructor.cs:80-85 sees single.StartsWith("[") -> JToken.Parse -> JArray. The existing multi-row CLR proof exists (TypedSubmissionStorageTests.cs:451-492) but NO test pins the browser single-row case.

findings.claim: A write-time flag alone does NOT fix the live Oqtane bug: on read, TypedFieldValues is rebuilt purely from DB value rows, carrying no shape flag; the reconstructor only sees SubmissionFieldRecord + value lists. A correct marker must be persisted or inferred from persisted metadata.

findings.evidence: Comment-only doc at TypedSubmissionStorageTests.cs:456-458. String/LongText reconstruct via Collapse<T> where count==1 returns the scalar not a List: SubmissionDataReconstructor.cs:66-71 — a single-selection MultiSelect/Checkbox-group reconstructs as a scalar string, same bug class.

findings.claim: Real-world exposure is narrow today, which lowers the urgency of a schema change: the trigger is Oqtane-collapse=true + a programmatic/SDK submission carrying a genuine CLR List with exactly one grid row; DNN keeps DataJson and most consumers still read DataJson.
findings.evidence: DnnSubmissionDataStore.cs:18,33 `SupportsDataJsonCollapse => false` (DNN readers consume DataJson); MEMORY backlog notes reports/CSV/workflow STILL read DataJson (reader-switch pending). Browser path proven unaffected above.

design.recommendation: Choose Option B now, with a concrete deliverable that satisfies the owner's "accept-with-browser-proof + documented (not comment-only)" bar, and pre-design Option A to ship at the reader-switch milestone. Rationale tied to blast radius: (1) The only CORRECT form of Option A that fixes the live Oqtane path requires either a persisted IsCollection column on MF_SubmissionFields — threaded through the EF model, a new Oqtane migration, the DNN SqlDataProvider ALTER, all three host stores' insert/read, and the reconstructor — or a FieldType-classifier in the reconstructor. A flag added only to SubmissionFieldWrite/TypedFieldValues would pass the in-memory unit test while leaving the real bug intact (TypedFieldValues is rebuilt from DB rows on read). (2) The typed-storage phase is explicitly unfinished (Umbraco twin, reader-switch, backfill wiring all pending); adding a schema column mid-phase risks a half-wired column, and the same stores/migration will be reopened at reader-switch anyway — do the migration once, then. (3) Today the defect is latent: browser forms never trigger it, DNN keeps DataJson, and consumers still read DataJson, so no user-visible data is currently wrong. (4) Option B is near-zero blast radius and directly answers the owner: add the missing browser-stringified-array-single-row JArray round-trip test (positive proof the happy path is safe), add an executable pin-test asserting the current server-side-CLR-single-row JObject behavior (turns the limitation from a comment into a spec, and value is proven not lost — only shape), and record the limitation + its eventual fix in the handoff and MEMORY backlog. If the owner insists on a code fix immediately, the lowest-blast-radius correct option is Option A2 (reconstructor consults the already-persisted FieldType, one-file change, no migration) — accept its caveat that File single-object vs multi-file stays JObject-for-one and that it introduces a type-based notion of collection-ness distinct from the write-time truth. The robust Option A1 (persisted IsCollection) is the design to adopt at reader-switch.

design.title: R3-J Deployment-Trap Remediation Plan: Clean-Build Pack, Single-Source Versioning, Post-Pack Guard, Runtime Health Endpoint
design.summary: R3-J is confirmed as the highest release risk. Two independent gaps combine: (1) the lean pack path `MegaForm.Oqtane.Package/release.cmd` runs `nuget pack` with NO build at all, so it ships whatever stale DLLs already sit in `bin/Release`; and (2) the five artifacts that must agree on a version do not — nuspec 1.7.107, ModuleInfo 1.7.108, Server/Client csproj 1.7.15, Package csproj 1.7.22, Core csproj 1.5.0. The new Core contract member `ISubmissionDataStore.SupportsDataJsonCollapse` is called by `SubmissionProcessor` inside a fail-soft try/catch, so a stale Core.dll next to a new Server.dll throws `MissingMethodException` that is swallowed — typed write/collapse silently dies while the package looks installed. This trap already bit once (submission 52 kept full DataJson). The fix is a clean Release build of Core+Server+Client+Shared before pack (both net9.0 and net10.0 for Core), a single version source feeding nuspec + ModuleInfo, a post-pack nupkg validator that fails the build on stale/missing/mismatched DLLs, and an admin-only runtime diagnostics endpoint that proves loaded assembly versions, the resolved data store, collapse state, and a typed-write smoke.

findings.claim: The lean release script packs with no build — it is the actual R3-J trap. It only deletes old nupkgs and calls nuget pack, so it ships whatever DLLs already exist in bin/Release, no matter how stale.

design.recommendation: Do R3-J before any package install/push. Ship four things: (1) make release.cmd delegate to a hardened pack.cmd that does a CLEAN Release build of Shared+Core(net9.0 AND net10.0)+Client+Server before nuget pack; (2) put the version in one file (version.props + version.txt) that feeds csproj <Version>, the nuspec version via `nuget pack -Version`, and a pre-build assert that ModuleInfo.Version equals it (and is present in ReleaseVersions); (3) add a post-pack validator (a small net10 console using MetadataLoadContext) that unzips the nupkg and fails the build unless every lib\netX contains all four MegaForm DLLs, Core.dll exposes ISubmissionDataStore.SupportsDataJsonCollapse, Server.Oqtane.dll's referenced MegaForm.Core version equals the packed Core.dll AssemblyVersion, the nupkg version equals ModuleInfo.Version, and all packed DLL mtimes are newer than the newest tracked .cs source; (4) add an admin/host-only GET diagnostics endpoint that returns loaded assembly versions+paths, whether ISubmissionDataStore resolved and its concrete type, SupportsDataJsonCollapse, a runtime reflection check that the loaded Core actually has the member, and an opt-in self-cleaning typed-write smoke. Then sequence the remaining P0s dependency-first: R3-J -> R3-A -> R3-B -> R3-C -> R3-D -> R3-E. R3-A (Umbraco/Web: add typed store or explicitly mark legacy-only with SupportsDataJsonCollapse=false) first because it makes the platform contract truthful and stops accidental collapse on hosts with no hydration. R3-B (Core reader facade + replace direct _subRepo.Insert bypasses in WorkflowEngine/ConfiguredAppStarter) next because those bypasses create master rows with no typed field rows, corrupting everything built on top. R3-C (typed SetField/UpdateFields + workflow sync across hosts) after B because it needs the unified typed-write command path B establishes. R3-D (SDK Data/Fields facade) after C because the public SDK surface should freeze only once the field-level mutation API exists. R3-E (backfill wiring + migrated marker + verification counts) last of the P0s because it operates on the whole existing corpus and can only be trusted once A/B/C provide correct typed write+read on every host. Note: the audit groups A/C/D/E together and puts B after; the dependency-first order above pulls B forward because its direct-writer bypasses are a correctness hole under A, C, D, and E.

The real narrower defects: (a) no dotnet clean anywhere, so it is incremental; (b) pack.cmd:171-172 explicitly copies net9.0 Core.dll into Server bin but has NO net10.0 equivalent. Since the live Oqtane runs net10.0 (per memory), the concern is actually more relevant to net10 than the design frames it.

C3 (deploy-gate claim speculative): 'nuspec-vs-ModuleInfo patch difference mis-fires the deploy gate' is unsubstantiated. In Oqtane the upgrade/schema gate is driven by ModuleDefinition.Version (ModuleInfo.cs:12=1.7.108) + ReleaseVersions (:14); the nuspec <version> (1.7.107) is the NuGet package version in Module Management. (2) doc.Values.Count is invalid - SubmissionDataDocument (SubmissionDataDocument.cs:10-22) exposes Data, Fields, FieldValues but NO Values property; must be doc.Data.Count or doc.Fields.Count.

C5 (auth convention deviation): the sketch uses [Authorize(Roles=RoleNames.Host)] but the controller's established pattern is [Authorize(Policy="EditModule"/"ViewModule")] + a CanUseAdminPopup() gate (MegaFormController.cs:44-45; Reports.cs:50/82/193 pair [Authorize] with CanUseAdminPopup()). Host-only is a defensible stricter choice for diagnostics, but the design should either follow the existing policy+CanUseAdminPopup convention or justify the deviation.
